entities.summary: Andrés Luna y Pardo de Tavera was a French-hispanofilipino architect who built the first air-conditioned building in the Philippines, the Crystal Arcade which was the seat of the pre-war Manila Stock Exchange that was once located on No. 71 Escolta Street, Binondo, Manila. He was assigned as the city architect of the City of Manila from 1920 to 1924. Some of his buildings were lost during World War II.
